changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 2 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6213-core-adapters-readme-owns-its-directory.md`

- names `packages/core/src/adapters/README.md` → `packages/core/src/adapters/README.md` — edited by this change

  > `packages/core/src/adapters/README.md` now documents the adapters that are actually in that directory, and the ObjectStack material it carried moved to the package that owns the behaviour (objectui#6213). Both files ship to consumers — `@object-ui/core` publishes its `src/`, and a README rides every tarball — so this was published documentation describing the wrong package.

### `.changeset/8976-icontains-lowers-in-converter.md`

- names `packages/core/src/adapters/README.md` → `packages/core/src/adapters/README.md` — edited by this change

  > `$icontains` is a member of `@objectstack/spec`'s `FILTER_OPERATORS`, `ValueDataSource` executes it, `FilterConditionField` emits it for its "contains (ignore case)" builder row, and `packages/core/src/adapters/README.md` prescribes it as the repair when `$like` / `$ilike` / `$regex` are refused. `convertOperatorToAST` had no row for it, so the ObjectStack lowering path answered a `FilterOperatorError` (`code: 'INVALID_FILTER'`, `httpStatus: 400`) with the generic unknown-operator paragraph — the one spelling this repo tells an author to write was the one spelling it rejected. An admin who picked "contains (ignore case)" in the filter builder authored criteria that the in-memory matcher honoured and the ObjectStack data source refused.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `b5b6f3753` (merge-base with origin/main): 9 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1579 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2167 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36317633601)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `451ac493aa91b1f13db105bdbda89b12447199dd`

### ① Derived judgments

**The lowering is the one lowering.** `find`'s array arm calls `toFilterNodeSafely` (`packages/core/src/utils/filter-converter.ts`), the same export `ObjectGrid`, `ListView`, `ObjectView`, `RelatedList`, `LineItemsPanel`, `related-count-store`, `element-data-source`, `drill-down`, `RecordPickerDialog`, `PeoplePicker`, `LookupField` and `ElementDataSourceGate` call (12 real callers by symbol, re-derived; four further grep hits are prose only). The adapter adds no operator table: `viewFilterRuleToNode` folds through the spec's `normalizeFilterOperator` and the matcher's existing `canonicalAstOperator`. Nuance the PR body already records: the wire adapter has its own pre-existing fold (`FILTER_OPERATOR_ALIASES` / `toAstFilterOperator` in `data-objectstack`), so the family has two lowerings, neither added here.

**Operator sweep, 20 OF 20 agree.** Every member of `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS` at objectstack main `805af4f290` (equals, not_equals, contains, not_contains, icontains, starts_with, ends_with, greater_than, less_than, greater_than_or_equal, less_than_or_equal, in, not_in, is_empty, is_not_empty, is_null, is_not_null, before, after, between) was sent as a rule array through `ValueDataSource.find` over 4 rows and compared with the object-bound arm: the same array through `ObjectStackAdapter.find` (fake fetch), the `filter` query param read back, `parseFilterAST`, then `@objectstack/formula`'s `matchesFilterCondition`. Identical id sets on all 20, zero warnings. Every canonical view spelling is a key of the spec's `AST_OPERATOR_MAP`.

**Acceptance, and where it is lenient.**
- Alias `eq` and camelCase `greaterThan`: accepted, folded by the spec (spec-legal).
- Missing `operator`, and `op` key: adapter refuses ("filter node [status,null,open] is not a shape the matcher reads", 0 rows, 1 warn); the wire defaults to equality. Adapter is the louder face; spec requires `operator`.
- Mixed array, rule then tuple: adapter and wire agree (rows [1]). Mixed array, tuple then rule: adapter lowers both elements (rows [1]); the wire hands the array back verbatim (server 400); the spec's `filter` doors (`z.array(ViewFilterRuleSchema)`) refuse any mixed array. This is the one shape the adapter now reads that the object-bound arm refuses. It is inherited from `toFilterNode` (element-wise by design, for `ObjectView`'s rule-plus-URL-triple concatenation), not written here, and refusing it in the adapter would need a second discriminator; the pin "a rule mixed with an AST tuple lowers element-wise" enshrines sink parity, not spec legality. Recorded, not blocking.
- Rule nested two deep, `['and', ['or', rule, rule]]`: adapter refuses (2 warns, 0 rows), wire lowers recursively. Off-spec; adapter is stricter. The `matchesASTFilter` docblock sentence "A rule object that DOES arrive is one the lowering left alone — no string `field`" is therefore imprecise; suggested: "one the lowering left alone — no string `field`, or nested below the top level the sink maps —".
- Uppercase `EQUALS`: accepted by adapter and wire, refused by the spec enum; pre-existing AST-arm lowercasing, not introduced here.
- Genuinely unreadable node `[{ foo: 'bar' }]`: still refused with the byte-identical sentence "filter node [{"foo":"bar"}] is not a shape the matcher reads. Rows are excluded rather than passed through."
- Lowering refusals read once: "[ObjectUI] ValueDataSource: filter rule refused as it is lowered: The stored view rule on field 'status' carries an ARRAY … Rows are excluded rather than passed through." `find` did not throw on any probed input.

**Census.** Four unlowered inline callers confirmed by reading the arms: `ObjectMap.tsx`, `ObjectTree.tsx`, `ObjectCalendar.tsx` (each `new ValueDataSource` then `find('', { $filter: queryFilter, … })`) and `ObjectGantt.tsx` via `resolveDataSource(dataConfig, …)`; `resolveDataSource.ts` is at `packages/core/src/adapters/resolveDataSource.ts` as the dev says (card and triage misplace it). Only other non-test constructions: `plugin-designer` `ObjectManager.tsx` and `FieldDesigner.tsx`, which hand the adapter to `ObjectGrid`, which lowers via `toFilterNodeSafely` first. `useViewData` wraps `resolveDataSource` and has no in-tree caller. Double lowering is a no-op: `toFilterNode` applied twice equals once for a rule array, a flat AST, an `and` group, a bare tuple and a mixed array (probed).

**Pins, all runs under `os-verify-lock.sh` in a detached worktree at head, `--maxWorkers=2`.** Head: 5 pin files plus the 8769 suite plus my probe, 7 files, 40 OF 40 green. Base leg (adapter file swapped to blob `41edc7da69`, pins only): 5 failed files, 16 failed and 15 passed OF 31; the red set is exactly the 6 component rule-array cases and the 10 adapter cases the dev named; restored, blob `6cc8754cd37c` equals HEAD, diff empty. Ablation A (anchor `const lowered = toFilterNodeSafely(params.$filter);` to pass-through, blob to `2a83b68fdfc9`): 16 failed and 23 passed OF 39, same 16, 8769 all green; restored and proven. Ablation B (anchor `refuseFilterNode(refusals, loweringRefusalReason(lowered.refusal));` to `throw lowered.refusal;`, blob to `f6eea0f86e00`): 2 failed and 37 passed OF 39, exactly the two "does NOT throw" adapter pins; `refusedComparandDoesNotThrow` green; restored and proven. Final tree `dirty=0`. No pin is tautological; the empty-array control is asserted twice under two names (duplicate, both honest).

**Components end to end.** `ObjectMap` (data provider value, and staticData) and `ObjectCalendar` (staticData) plot 3 OF 5 rows at head and 0 on base; the calendar's `staticData` reaches the adapter through `resolveRecordSourceConfig`, which wraps it as provider value with items, then `inlineSource.find('', { $filter: queryFilter, … })`. Tree and gantt likewise 3 OF 5.

**Type-check.** `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core type-check` exits 0 at head after `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/core^...'` (a first attempt without the types dist failed on TS6305 only; environment, not the PR). CI Type Check is green.

### ② Semver level

`@object-ui/core: patch`, Clause-② no — correct. Export lines of `ValueDataSource.ts` are identical to base; `packages/core/src/index.ts`, `adapters/index.ts` and `package.json` are untouched; `loweringRefusalReason` is module-private. Plugins gain tests and one comment-only header, no bump needed; `Changeset Declaration` and `Changeset Bump Policy` green.

Changeset, README and docblocks read sentence by sentence: accurate. Verified specifically: "an empty array is no filter (as it is on the wire)" (`translateFilterToAST([])` is `undefined`); "an operator the spec does not know passes through VERBATIM" (`bogus` refused as its AST twin, pinned); the aliases and valueless `is_null` claims (probed). One imprecision noted above in the `matchesASTFilter` docblock. PR body: reproduction, census counts (4, 2, 12), the two-sink asymmetry, the `entry.op ?? '='` observation and the objectstack#17321 / PR #20175 landing condition are all consistent with what I measured; the `os validate` green claim is the card's, not re-derived. The 8769 header repair is accurate: its `[['subject','icontains','']]` tuple passes the sink untouched and is judged by the matcher's comparand door; the base sentence "never the converter" was indeed made false. Observation: `ObjectGantt.tsx`'s untouched comment "The matcher is LOCAL: it never reaches `convertFiltersToAST`" stays literally true (the array arm never calls that function) but "LOCAL" is now loose; not blocking.
